termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a write-optimized storage structure that buffers writes in memory before flushing sorted files to disk.

q_en: Complete the write pattern of time-series storage.

q: 把 Metrics Monitoring 最终方案的核心决策链排好序：
steps: Query Service 用 rollups、缓存和查询拆分服务 dashboard
Agent 本地采集、缓冲和批量发送指标
Notification Service 对 alert event 做去重、分组、静默和重试
Ingestion Service 校验、控制 cardinality，并写入 Kafka
消费者写入 TSDB；Alert Evaluator 轮询或 Flink 流式评估规则
why: 最终架构把高吞吐写入、专用时序存储、低延迟查询、可靠告警和通知管理拆成清晰链路。
why_en: The final architecture separates edge batching, ingestion control, Kafka buffering, time-series storage, query optimization, alerting, and notification management.
tradeoff: 分层解耦（agent/kafka/tsdb/query/alert/notify）带来的可扩展性 vs 组件数量增加的运维复杂度
diagram:
flowchart LR
A[Agents] --> I[Ingestion]
I --> C[Cardinality Controls]
C --> K[Kafka]
K --> W[Storage Consumers]
W --> T[(TSDB)]
T --> Q[Query Service]
T --> E[Alert Evaluator]
K --> F[Flink Alerts]
E --> N[Notification Service]
F --> N
Q --> D[Dashboards]
N --> P[PagerDuty/Slack]
q_en: Put the core decision chain for the final Metrics Monitoring design in order.

scenario: 监控平台停摆 5 分钟，Kafka 里积压了 5 分钟指标；集群常态跑在 75% 容量，追平这段积压要 15 分钟。
scenario_en: The platform was down five minutes, leaving five minutes of metrics backed up in Kafka; the cluster normally runs at seventy-five percent capacity, so catching up would take fifteen minutes.
q: 这段追不完的积压该怎么处理？
q_en: How should the platform handle a backlog it cannot catch up on?
options: 临时扩容到能追平为止，不惜任何代价
跳过部分积压尽快回到实时，接受丢数据
边追赶边暂停 dashboard 与告警的全部查询
把积压整段转存冷存储，稍后离线补写回来
options_en: Scale up temporarily until the backlog is fully caught up, whatever it costs.
Skip part of the backlog to return to real time, accepting data loss.
Keep catching up while pausing all dashboard and alerting queries.
Dump the whole backlog to cold storage and backfill it offline later.
optionExplanations: 按 15 分钟追平算要临时翻倍算力，而事故期间正是最难拿到额外容量的时候。
监控的价值在于反映此刻；先回到实时，再承认这段窗口的历史数据缺了一块。
停掉查询等于在事故中主动关灯，追赶省下的那点算力换不来这个代价。
离线补写要再建一条回填链路，补回来的旧点对正在进行的排查也没有帮助。
optionExplanations_en: Catching up in fifteen minutes means roughly doubling capacity, and an incident is exactly when spare capacity is hardest to get.
Monitoring is valuable because it reflects now, so you return to real time and accept a hole in that window of history.
Pausing queries means turning the lights off during an incident; the compute you save is not worth that.
Offline backfill needs a whole second pipeline, and the recovered old points do not help the investigation happening now.
why: 监控的用处是反映当下：长期落后的数据救不了正在发生的事故，还持续占着追赶容量。代价是这段窗口的历史永久缺失。
why_en: Monitoring only helps if it reflects the present, so when you cannot catch up you skip ahead and accept a hole in history rather than run behind forever.
tradeoff: 历史数据完整性 vs 实时新鲜度
whenOtherWins: 如果这些指标还要用于计费或合规审计，正确性优先，就必须补齐积压而不能丢弃。

termDefinitions.meaning: 积压：停机期间没被消费的消息堆在队列里，恢复后要额外时间才能处理完。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A backlog is the pile of unconsumed messages that builds up during downtime and must be worked off after recovery.

scenario: Kafka topic 的保留期设为 6 小时，写 TSDB 的消费者集群整体故障，8 小时后才修好重新消费。
scenario_en: The Kafka topic keeps six hours of retention, and the consumer cluster that writes to the TSDB stayed down for eight hours before it was repaired.
q: 这 8 小时的指标最终会怎样？
q_en: What ultimately happens to those eight hours of metrics?
options: Kafka 自动延长保留期，直到所有消费者都追平
最早那 2 小时被保留策略删掉，永久找不回来
消费者恢复后可以从 offset 0 完整回放全部数据
数据自动挪去冷存储，等消费者恢复后再回补上
options_en: Kafka automatically extends retention until every consumer has caught up.
The oldest two hours are deleted by the retention policy and are gone for good.
After recovery consumers can replay everything from offset zero.
The data moves to cold storage and is backfilled once consumers recover.
optionExplanations: 保留期是 broker 上的静态配置，它按时间删段，不会去看有没有消费者落后。
停机 8 小时超出 6 小时窗口，最早的 2 小时先被删，之后没有任何副本可读。
offset 0 早已随旧段被清理，能读到的最早位置是当前还活着的那个段。
Kafka 不会自己分层归档，想要冷存储必须另建一条消费者链路提前落盘。
optionExplanations_en: Retention is a static broker setting that deletes segments by age; it never checks whether a consumer is lagging.
Eight hours of downtime exceeds the six-hour window, so the oldest two hours are deleted first and no copy remains.
Offset zero was cleaned up with the old segments; the earliest readable position is whatever segment is still alive.
Kafka does not tier data on its own; cold storage requires a separate consumer that persists messages ahead of time.
why: 正常时消费者紧跟队尾读；停摆后 offset 原地不动而 broker 仍按 6 小时删旧段；恢复后只能从最早存活的 offset 读起，超窗的 2 小时永久缺失。
why_en: Consumers normally read the tail, but while they are down the broker keeps deleting six-hour-old segments, so they resume at the oldest surviving offset and the excess is gone.
diagram:
flowchart LR
A[Consumers read tail] --> B[Consumers die, offset frozen]
B --> C[Broker deletes segments older than 6h]
C --> D[Recovery: resume at earliest live offset]
D --> E[2h of metrics permanently lost]

termDefinitions.meaning: 偏移量：消费者在一个 Kafka 分区里读到的位置编号，故障期间它不会自动前进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is the position number a consumer has reached inside a Kafka partition, and it does not advance while the consumer is down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保留期：broker 保存消息段的时长，超时的段会被删除，与消费进度无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retention is how long a broker keeps message segments before deleting them, regardless of how far consumers have read.

scenario: TSDB 写入短暂变慢、通知渠道也在抖动，团队要为这类故障定一条统一的降级原则。
scenario_en: TSDB writes briefly slow down and the notification channel is flaky, so the team needs one degradation principle for this class of failure.
q: 监控系统坏掉时应该优先牺牲什么？
q_en: What should a monitoring system sacrifice first when things break?
options: 牺牲新鲜度，但不让在途数据消失
牺牲告警正确性，先把端到端延迟压到最低
牺牲存储成本，把每个点同步双写到三个副本
为了立刻看到实时图，直接清空 agent 和队列缓冲
options_en: Sacrifice freshness, but never let in-flight data disappear.
Sacrifice alert correctness to push end-to-end latency as low as possible.
Sacrifice storage cost by synchronously writing every point to three replicas.
Clear the agent and queue buffers so the live view comes back immediately.
optionExplanations: agent 本地缓冲、Kafka 跨区复制、幂等写让每一步都能续跑，数据只是晚到。
告警错了比晚了更糟：一次误报或漏报会直接让值班对整套系统失去信任。
同步三副本是在换持久性，跟「故障时先放弃哪一项」不在同一个取舍轴上。
清空缓冲确实立刻恢复实时，但被丢掉的点正是事故当时最该看的证据。
optionExplanations_en: Local agent buffering, cross-zone Kafka replication, and idempotent writes keep every stage resumable, so data merely arrives late.
A wrong alert is worse than a late one; one false page or miss destroys on-call trust in the whole platform.
Synchronous triple-writing trades cost for durability, which is a different axis from what to give up during a failure.
Dropping the buffers does restore the live view instantly, but the discarded points are exactly the evidence the incident needs.
why: 指标和告警可以晚到，但不能消失；缓冲、复制和幂等写把故障变成延迟。代价是恢复期里看到的图是滞后的。
why_en: Metrics and alerts may arrive late but must not vanish, so buffering, replication, and idempotent writes turn failures into delay, at the cost of a lagging view during recovery.
tradeoff: 新鲜度 vs 正确性
whenOtherWins: 如果积压长到永远追不平，就要反过来主动丢掉一段数据，用它换回实时性。

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一条数据重复写入多次结果与写一次相同，因此重试不会产生重复点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent write produces the same result no matter how many times it is retried, so retries never create duplicate points.

termDefinitions.meaning: 已经离开来源、但还没落到最终存储的那批数据，例如缓冲区和队列里的点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-flight data is data that has left its source but has not yet landed in final storage, such as points sitting in buffers and queues.

scenario: 500k 台服务器要接入平台。pull 指中心定时去每台机器抓指标，push 指每台机器上的 agent 主动上报；约束是摄取层短暂故障时不能丢点。
scenario_en: Five hundred thousand servers must be onboarded. Pull means a central scraper periodically fetches from each machine; push means an agent on each machine reports in. The constraint is that a brief ingestion outage must lose no points.
q: 这个约束下该选哪种采集模型？
q_en: Which collection model wins under that constraint?
options: pull：中心统一控制抓取节奏，故障后自动重抓
push：agent 本地缓冲重试，摄取层恢复后补发
pull：中心抓取的采集延迟必然低于 agent 上报
两者等价，只取决于团队更熟悉哪一套工具链
options_en: Pull, because a central scraper controls the cadence and re-scrapes after a failure.
Push, because agents buffer locally and resend once the ingestion layer recovers.
Pull, because centrally scraped collection latency is necessarily lower than reporting.
They are equivalent; it only depends on which toolchain the team knows better.
optionExplanations: 中心挂掉那几个周期根本没人去抓，数据在源头就没生成，事后无从重抓。
agent 把点先攒在本机，摄取层恢复后再批量发出，故障期只变成延迟。
两种模型的延迟都取决于采集间隔和批量大小，跟谁发起请求没必然关系。
本设计要求故障期不丢点，这一条就足以把两者分开，不是口味问题。
optionExplanations_en: While the central scraper is down nobody fetches those cycles at all, so the data never exists and cannot be re-scraped later.
The agent accumulates points on the host and flushes them in batches once ingestion recovers, turning the outage into mere delay.
Latency in both models comes from the collection interval and batch size, not from who initiates the request.
The requirement that no points are lost during an outage already separates the two models; this is not a matter of taste.
why: pull 模型下中心不在就没人采集，那几个周期的数据从未存在；push 把缓冲推到边缘，代价是要在 500k 台机器上运维 agent。
why_en: With pull, nothing is collected while the scraper is down and those cycles never exist; push buffers at the edge, at the cost of running agents on half a million machines.
tradeoff: 中心统一控制 vs 边缘缓冲带来的抗故障能力
whenOtherWins: 目标机器数量很小、又不允许装 agent（例如托管中间件只暴露一个指标端口）时，pull 更省事。

scenario: 订单骤降是最重要的事故信号，但按 5 分钟窗口数订单数波动很大，要攒够数据才敢报，慢了好几分钟。
scenario_en: A drop in orders is the most important incident signal, but counting orders over a five-minute window is noisy and needs enough data before it can fire, costing several minutes.
q: 怎么设计指标才能近乎即时地发现订单下跌？
q_en: How do you design a metric that catches an order drop almost instantly?
options: 监控「距上次订单的毫秒数」这个稳定量
把订单数的告警阈值调低，让更小的跌幅也触发
把评估间隔从 5 分钟改成 1 秒，其余全都不变
对订单数做 30 天移动平均之后再去比较同比
options_en: Track milliseconds since the last order, which is a very stable quantity.
Lower the threshold on order count so smaller dips also fire.
Change the evaluation interval from five minutes to one second, nothing else.
Take a thirty-day moving average of order count and compare year over year.
optionExplanations: 订单极密集时这个间隔几乎恒定，订单一停它立刻线性上涨，不用攒窗口。
阈值调低只会让本来就抖动的计数更频繁误报，噪音换不来更早的判断。
评估更频繁但底层还是同一个噪音大的计数，早报出来的多半是假警报。
移动平均刻意抹平短期波动，正好把「刚刚停单」这种突变延后才暴露。
optionExplanations_en: When orders are dense this gap is nearly constant, and the moment orders stop it climbs linearly with no window to accumulate.
A lower threshold just makes an already noisy count fire more often; noise does not buy an earlier true judgement.
Evaluating more often still reads the same noisy counter, so what fires earlier is mostly false alarms.
A moving average deliberately smooths short-term swings, which is exactly what delays a sudden stop from showing up.
why: 订单量足够大时「距上次订单的毫秒数」方差极小，异常一发生就单调上涨，无需窗口聚合。代价是它只对高频事件成立。
why_en: At huge order volume, milliseconds since the last order barely varies and climbs the moment orders stop, so nothing needs to accumulate — but only high-frequency events work.
tradeoff: 指标的稳定性 vs 适用范围（只对高频事件成立）
whenOtherWins: 事件本来就稀疏时（比如每小时几单），间隔天然抖动，还是得回到窗口聚合的阈值告警。

termDefinitions.meaning: 取最近一段时间的均值来平滑噪音，代价是对突变的响应变慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A moving average smooths noise by averaging a recent time span, at the cost of reacting slowly to sudden changes.

scenario: cpu_usage 已经带 host 标签，500k 台服务器对应 500k 条 series。现在再加一个 region 标签，而每台机器只属于一个 region。
scenario_en: The cpu_usage metric already carries a host label, giving five hundred thousand series for five hundred thousand servers. Now a region label is added, and each machine belongs to exactly one region.
q: 加了 region 标签后 series 数会怎么变？
q_en: How does the series count change after adding the region label?
options: 仍是 500k：只有真实出现的组合才算 series
变成 500k 乘以 region 数，每个组合都会建一条
直接翻倍，因为新旧两套标签会各存一份 series
series 数不变，但每条 series 的数据点数会翻倍
options_en: Still five hundred thousand: only combinations that actually occur count as series.
It becomes five hundred thousand times the number of regions, one per combination.
It doubles, because the old and new label sets each store their own series.
The series count is unchanged but each series holds twice as many points.
optionExplanations: server-1 只在 us-east 出现，就不存在 server-1 在 us-west 的那条 series。
笛卡尔积是理论上限，实际只有真被上报过的组合才会在存储里建出来。
旧标签没有被保留成第二套，同一个点只按它当前的完整标签集算一条。
标签影响的是有多少条 series，不改变每条 series 上采样点的密度。
optionExplanations_en: Server-1 only ever appears in us-east, so a series for server-1 in us-west simply never exists.
The Cartesian product is a theoretical ceiling; only combinations that are actually reported get created in storage.
The old label set is not kept as a second copy; each point counts once under its current full label set.
Labels change how many series exist, not how densely each series is sampled.
why: series = metric 名 + 标签的唯一组合，只有真实出现过的组合才计数。所以容量规划要按实际组合数估，不能拿标签取值的笛卡尔积吓自己。
why_en: A series is one unique combination of metric name and labels, and only combinations that really occur count, so plan capacity from real combinations, not the Cartesian product.

termDefinitions.meaning: 时间序列：一个 metric 名加一组标签的唯一组合，随时间记录一串(时间戳, 值)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A series is one unique combination of metric name and labels, recording a sequence of timestamp-value pairs over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把各标签所有取值两两组合出的全部可能，是基数的理论上限而非实际值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Cartesian product is every possible combination of all label values, which is the theoretical ceiling of cardinality rather than the real count.

scenario: 平台上有 1 万条 alert rule，用户几周才改一次，但 evaluator 每 15 秒就要把全部规则取出来评估一轮。
scenario_en: The platform holds ten thousand alert rules that users change only every few weeks, while the evaluator pulls all of them every fifteen seconds to evaluate.
q: rule store 该按什么读写特征来选型？
q_en: What read-write profile should the rule store be chosen for?
options: 按写吞吐选，规则写入才是这里的主要负载
读多写极少，规则可整体缓存进 evaluator 内存
按时序压缩率选，把规则和指标点放进同一个 TSDB
按跨区强一致选，每轮评估都必须做线性一致读
options_en: Optimise for write throughput, since rule writes are the dominant load here.
Read-heavy and write-rare, so rules can be cached wholesale in evaluator memory.
Optimise for time-series compression and store rules in the same TSDB as points.
Optimise for cross-region strong consistency with a linearizable read every cycle.
optionExplanations: 规则按周变更，写入量小到可以忽略，为它优化等于优化最不痛的那一端。
普通 Postgres 存权威规则，evaluator 定期刷进内存，评估就不再打数据库。
规则是小体量配置数据，没有时间序列形状，塞进 TSDB 拿不到压缩收益。
规则晚生效几十秒完全可接受，为此付线性一致读的代价没有对应收益。
optionExplanations_en: Rules change weekly, so write volume is negligible and optimising for it targets the least painful end.
Plain Postgres holds the authoritative rules while the evaluator periodically refreshes them into memory, keeping evaluation off the database.
Rules are small configuration records with no time-series shape, so a TSDB yields no compression benefit.
A rule taking tens of seconds to take effect is fine, so paying for linearizable reads buys nothing.
why: 写按周计而评估按秒计（1 万条 × 每 15 秒 ≈ 670 次查询/秒），所以选普通关系库加内存缓存。代价是规则改动要等一个缓存刷新窗口才生效。
why_en: Writes land weekly while evaluations land every few seconds, so a plain relational store plus an in-memory cache wins, at the cost of a refresh window before edits apply.
tradeoff: 规则变更的生效延迟 vs 评估路径的读放大
whenOtherWins: 如果规则改由自动化系统每秒批量改写，写路径就成了主负载，缓存策略必须重做。

termDefinitions.meaning: 时序数据库：为按时间追加写和时间范围扫描优化的专用存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB, or time-series database, is storage specialised for append-only writes ordered by time and for time-range scans.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证读到的一定是最新已提交的写，代价是跨副本协调带来的额外延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A linearizable read guarantees you see the latest committed write, at the cost of extra cross-replica coordination latency.

scenario: 每台服务器每 10 秒产生 100 个点，合计 5M 点/秒打向中心；其中 latency 指标的用户只关心 p99。
scenario_en: Each server emits one hundred points every ten seconds, five million points per second in total toward the centre, and users of the latency metric only care about p99.
q: agent 侧该怎么减少上报量？
q_en: How should the agent reduce what it ships?
options: 本地先算好百分位，只上报聚合后的结果
把采集频率从每 10 秒一次降到每 5 分钟一次
每个点单独同步 POST 到中心，让中心去做聚合
本地随机采样 1% 的点，其余的直接扔掉不报
options_en: Compute percentiles locally and ship only the aggregated result.
Drop the collection frequency from every ten seconds to every five minutes.
Synchronously POST every single point and let the centre aggregate.
Randomly sample one percent of points locally and discard the rest.
optionExplanations: 聚合在边缘做完，中心收到的是每台机器一个 p99，而不是背后的原始点流。
降频省了量也砸了分辨率，10 秒粒度的尖峰在 5 分钟采样下会整个消失。
这正是要避免的形态：5M 点就是 5M 次请求，中心先被连接数压垮。
随机采样对计数类勉强可用，但对尾部分位数会系统性低估最慢那批请求。
optionExplanations_en: Aggregation finishes at the edge, so the centre receives one p99 per machine instead of the raw stream behind it.
Lowering frequency saves volume but destroys resolution; a spike visible at ten seconds vanishes at five-minute sampling.
This is exactly the shape to avoid: five million points means five million requests, crushing the centre on connections alone.
Random sampling is tolerable for counters but systematically underestimates tail percentiles, which are the slowest requests.
why: 把聚合推到边缘后中心只收约 50k 请求/秒，而不是 500k 台 × 100 点 ÷ 10 秒 = 5M 点/秒。代价是原始点不再上报，事后换个分位数就算不出来了。
why_en: Aggregating at the edge leaves the centre about fifty thousand requests per second instead of five hundred thousand hosts times one hundred points every ten seconds.
tradeoff: 上报量 vs 原始数据的可回溯性
whenOtherWins: 需要事后任意切片或重算成别的分位数时，只能把原始点送到中心存下来。

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位：99% 的请求都比它快，用来描述尾部延迟而不是平均水平。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: P99 is the ninety-ninth percentile, the value that ninety-nine percent of requests beat, describing tail latency rather than the average.

scenario: 团队决定在全部 500k 台服务器上部署采集 agent，把批量和预聚合推到边缘，而平台团队只有 5 个人。
scenario_en: The team decides to deploy a collection agent on all five hundred thousand servers to push batching and pre-aggregation to the edge, while the platform team has five people.
q: 这个决定带来的主要新增运维负担是什么？
q_en: What new operational burden does that decision create?
options: Kafka 的分区数从此必须等于服务器的台数
要统一管起 500k 份 agent 的版本、配置和故障
中心 ingestion 服务的实例数必须同步扩到 500k 个
TSDB 的原始数据保留期必须缩短到 1 天以内
options_en: The Kafka partition count must now equal the number of servers.
You must manage versions, configuration, and failures for half a million agents.
The central ingestion service must scale to five hundred thousand instances too.
Raw retention in the TSDB must be shortened to under one day.
optionExplanations: 分区数按吞吐和消费并行度定，跟有多少台机器在上报没有绑定关系。
agent 本身就是一套跑在 50 万个节点上的分布式软件，发版和排障都要有流程。
agent 批量上报后中心请求量降到约 50k/秒，实例数反而是变少而不是变多。
保留期由查询需求和存储成本决定，跟采集端换成 agent 没有因果关系。
optionExplanations_en: Partition count follows throughput and consumer parallelism, not how many machines happen to report.
The agent is itself distributed software running on half a million nodes, and rollout plus debugging both need process.
Batching drops central traffic to about fifty thousand requests per second, so instance count goes down, not up.
Retention is set by query needs and storage cost; switching to agents does not cause it to change.
why: agent 把批量和聚合推到边缘，换来中心只收约 50k 请求/秒；代价是多出一支跑在 500k 个节点上的软件要发版、配置和排障。
why_en: Agents buy the centre a drop to roughly fifty thousand requests per second by batching at the edge, and the price is owning software that runs on five hundred thousand nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跑在每台被监控机器上的采集进程，负责本地采集、缓冲、批量并上报。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An agent, or collector, is a process on each monitored machine that gathers, buffers, batches, and ships metrics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式持久消息队列，这里挡在摄取与存储之间吸收写入尖峰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed durable message queue, used here between ingestion and storage to absorb write spikes.

scenario: 先用 Postgres 单表存指标点，写不动之后按 metric 名哈希分成 32 个分片。用户仍要查「us-east 所有 pod 的平均 CPU」。
scenario_en: Metric points started in a single Postgres table and were then hashed by metric name into thirty-two shards, while users still ask for average CPU across all pods in us-east.
q: 分片之后这类 dashboard 查询会出什么问题？
q_en: What breaks about that dashboard query once the table is sharded?
options: 写入吞吐不会提升，分片只对读路径有效果
跨分片聚合要应用层自己扇出、汇总再排序
分片之后所有索引会自动失效，必须全部重建
每个分片都得保存全量数据，磁盘占用翻 32 倍
options_en: Write throughput does not improve, because sharding only helps reads.
Cross-shard aggregation must be fanned out, merged, and re-sorted by the application.
All indexes are invalidated by sharding and must be rebuilt from scratch.
Every shard must keep the full dataset, multiplying disk usage thirty-two times.
optionExplanations: 分片正是为了分摊写入，写吞吐会提升；坏掉的是原本一条 SQL 搞定的读。
数据散在 32 台机器上，单机 GROUP BY 不再成立，合并逻辑被推给了应用。
每个分片各自维护自己的索引，分片这个动作不会让索引整体作废。
哈希分片是把数据切开分配，不是复制全量；复制全量是副本要做的事。
optionExplanations_en: Sharding exists to spread writes, so write throughput improves; what breaks is the read that used to be one SQL statement.
Data now lives on thirty-two machines, so a single-node GROUP BY no longer holds and merge logic moves into the application.
Each shard keeps its own indexes; sharding does not invalidate them wholesale.
Hash sharding splits data across nodes rather than copying all of it; that is what replicas do.
why: 一条跨多个分片的聚合无法再由单机 SQL 完成，必须由应用扇出到 32 个分片、汇总再排序。代价是查询层变复杂，而且整体慢在最慢的那个分片上。
why_en: A cross-shard aggregation is no longer one SQL statement, so the app must fan out, merge, and re-sort, and the query is as slow as its slowest shard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个请求拆成多个子请求发往各分片，再把结果合并回来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means splitting one request into sub-requests sent to every shard and then merging the results back.

termDefinitions.meaning: SQL 里按某列分组再聚合的语法，前提是被聚合的数据都在同一个节点上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GROUP BY is the SQL clause that groups rows before aggregating, which assumes the rows all live on one node.

scenario: 隔壁团队的订单表也有 timestamp 列，他们看到本设计选了 InfluxDB，就想把订单库也换成时序库。
scenario_en: A neighbouring team notices their orders table also has a timestamp column and, seeing this design pick InfluxDB, wants to move their orders database to a time-series store too.
q: 什么条件下才真正需要专用时序库？
q_en: What actually justifies a dedicated time-series database?
options: 只要表里存在 timestamp 这一列就应该换过去
追加写为主、按时间范围扫描、旧数据整块过期
只要单表数据量超过 1TB 就应该换成时序库
需要事务、外键，并按订单 id 做精确点查的场景
options_en: Any table that has a timestamp column should move to one.
Append-mostly writes, time-range scans, and whole chunks of old data expiring.
Any table larger than one terabyte should move to a time-series database.
Workloads needing transactions, foreign keys, and exact point lookups by order id.
optionExplanations: 有时间戳只说明数据带时间，不代表访问模式是按时间扫描和整段淘汰。
这三条正是列式压缩、时间分区和整块 drop 能生效的前提，收益才成立。
数据量大先考虑分区和归档；体积本身不改变访问模式，也就不决定存储类型。
这恰恰是关系库的强项，换成时序库反而失去事务和外键这些约束能力。
optionExplanations_en: Having a timestamp only says the data is stamped, not that access is time-range scanning with bulk expiry.
Those three conditions are exactly what makes columnar compression, time partitioning, and dropping whole chunks pay off.
Large volume calls for partitioning and archiving; size alone does not change the access pattern or the storage type.
That is precisely a relational database strength, and a time-series store would give up transactions and foreign keys.
why: 时序库的优势建立在追加写、时间分区和列式压缩上；订单数据要改行、要事务、要按主键点查，换过去等于拿专用工具去干通用活。
why_en: Time-series stores win on append-only writes, time partitioning, and columnar compression, so order data needing updates and key lookups would be a misuse of a specialised tool.
tradeoff: 专用存储的写入与压缩优势 vs 通用关系库的事务和灵活查询
whenOtherWins: 订单这类要改行、要外键、要按主键精确点查的数据，Postgres 仍然是对的选择。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一列的值连续存放再压缩，时间戳和数值这类相似值压缩率极高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Columnar compression stores values of one column together before compressing, which works extremely well for similar values like timestamps.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按时间把数据切成块，查询只碰相关块，过期时整块删除而不逐行删。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time partitioning chunks data by time so queries touch only relevant chunks and expiry drops whole chunks instead of deleting rows.

scenario: 凌晨 3 点，一条 PagerDuty 页面发出后 15 分钟仍无人确认，事故还在扩大，而去重逻辑正压着同一条告警不再发。
scenario_en: At three in the morning a PagerDuty page has gone unacknowledged for fifteen minutes while the incident grows, and deduplication is suppressing repeats of the same alert.
q: Notification Service 这时应该做什么？
q_en: What should the Notification Service do at that point?
options: 按去重规则判定是同一条告警，继续静默不发
超过配置时限仍无 ack 就换渠道重新通知
每分钟重复推送同一条 page，直到有人回应
把这条告警自动标记成 resolved 然后直接关闭
options_en: Treat it as the same alert under dedup rules and stay silent.
Escalate to a different channel once the configured acknowledgement timeout passes.
Re-send the same page every minute until somebody responds.
Automatically mark the alert resolved and close it out.
optionExplanations: 去重压的是重复噪音，它压不掉「这个人没看见」这个完全不同的风险。
换渠道意味着换一条可能有人在看的路径，比在同一条死路上重试有意义。
同一渠道重复推送并没有提高被看见的概率，只是把噪音堆在同一个人身上。
没人 ack 不等于问题消失，自动 resolve 会把一次真实事故直接抹掉。
optionExplanations_en: Dedup suppresses repeat noise, but it does nothing about the completely different risk that nobody saw the page.
Switching channels tries a path somebody may actually be watching, unlike retrying down the same dead end.
Repeating on the same channel does not raise the odds of being seen; it just piles noise on one person.
No acknowledgement does not mean the problem is gone, and auto-resolving erases a real incident.
why: 去重解决重复噪音，escalation 解决「没人看见」：超时未 ack 就换一条渠道重发。代价是可能吵醒第二个人，制造额外打扰。
why_en: Deduplication handles repeat noise while escalation handles nobody looking, re-notifying on another channel after an acknowledgement timeout, at the cost of waking a second person.
tradeoff: 告警噪音 vs 漏看风险
whenOtherWins: 非紧急的 FYI 类通知不该升级，反复换渠道只会制造告警疲劳。

termDefinitions.meaning: 值班人手动确认「我看到了并在处理」的动作，是升级计时的终点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An acknowledgement is the on-call engineer manually confirming they have seen and are handling the alert, which stops the escalation timer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 升级：在配置的时限内没人确认时，改用另一条通知渠道再通知一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Escalation means re-notifying through a different channel when nobody acknowledges within a configured time.

scenario: 一个 30 天 panel 要扫 1000 条 series × 259,200 个点 ≈ 2.59 亿行、约 25GB，而一张 dashboard 通常有 6-10 个 panel，每个各发一次查询。
scenario_en: One thirty-day panel scans a thousand series times two hundred fifty-nine thousand points, about two hundred fifty-nine million rows or twenty-five gigabytes, and a dashboard typically holds six to ten panels each firing its own query.
q: 这个读放大最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: Which design judgement does that read amplification support?
options: 把 dashboard 的刷新间隔从 10 秒改成 1 秒即可
打开一次就是 6-10 个这种查询，必须靠 rollup 降点数
给 metrics 表再补一个 timestamp 索引就能解决问题
把每张 dashboard 限制成 1 个 panel，其余导出 CSV 离线看
options_en: Just change the dashboard refresh interval from ten seconds to one second.
One page load is six to ten such queries, so rollups must cut the point count.
Adding another timestamp index on the metrics table solves it.
Limit each dashboard to a single panel and export the rest to CSV for offline viewing.
optionExplanations: 刷得更勤只是把同样昂贵的扫描重复得更频繁，读压力反而被乘上去。
真正的负载单位是「一次打开」而不是「一条查询」，所以要在写侧先降点数。
索引能定位行，但 2.59 亿行本来就都要读进来做平均，扫描量一点没少。
砍功能是把成本转嫁给用户，事故排查时正需要几个 panel 并排对照。
optionExplanations_en: Refreshing more often just repeats the same expensive scan more frequently, multiplying read pressure.
The real unit of load is one page load, not one query, so the point count has to be cut on the write side.
An index locates rows, but all two hundred fifty-nine million rows still have to be read to average them.
Cutting features pushes cost onto users, and incident debugging is exactly when several panels side by side matter.
why: 扫描行数 = series 数 × 时间范围 ÷ 采样间隔 = 1000 × 30 天 ÷ 10 秒 ≈ 2.59 亿行 ≈ 25GB/panel，再乘 6-10 个 panel——这个乘数就是必须做预聚合 rollup 的依据。
why_en: Rows scanned equals series times range divided by sample interval — about twenty-five gigabytes per panel — and six to ten panels per load is what forces pre-computed rollups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预聚合：把细粒度点按更大时间桶提前算好（如 1 小时一档），查询时少扫很多点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rollup is a pre-computed aggregate over a coarser time bucket, so long-range queries scan far fewer points.

termDefinitions.meaning: 吉字节，约十亿字节，这里用来衡量一次查询要读进来的数据量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A gigabyte is roughly one billion bytes, used here to size how much data one query must read.

scenario: raw 10 秒数据保留 2 天，1 分钟 rollup 保留 2 周。用户查「最近 3 天」，时间范围正好跨过 2 天这条分辨率边界。
scenario_en: Raw ten-second data is kept for two days and one-minute rollups for two weeks, and a user queries the last three days, which crosses the two-day resolution boundary.
q: Query Service 必须做什么才能画出这条曲线？
q_en: What must the Query Service do to render that curve?
options: 直接拒绝跨边界的查询，要求用户改小时间范围
分段取两种粒度，对齐到同一个时间桶再拼接
一律退回 raw 数据，把这 3 天全部重新扫一遍
只返回 rollup 那一段，最近 2 天的数据直接省略
options_en: Reject queries that cross the boundary and ask the user to shrink the range.
Fetch both resolutions separately, align them to one bucket size, and stitch.
Fall back to raw data and rescan all three days at ten-second resolution.
Return only the rollup portion and omit the most recent two days.
optionExplanations: 跨边界是保留策略必然造成的常态，挡掉它等于让用户替存储分层背锅。
最近 2 天只有 raw、更早只有 1 分钟档，取完两段后统一 step 才不会画出断层。
超过 2 天的 raw 已经按保留策略删掉了，想退回也没有数据可以退。
省掉最近 2 天恰好丢的是最有用的一段，用户看图就是为了看现在。
optionExplanations_en: Crossing boundaries is the normal consequence of tiered retention, so rejecting it makes users pay for the storage layout.
The last two days exist only as raw and the older part only as one-minute rollups, so both are fetched and normalised to one step.
Raw data older than two days has already been deleted by retention, so there is nothing to fall back to.
Omitting the last two days drops precisely the most useful part, since users open the chart to see now.
why: 同一条曲线的两段来自不同分辨率，query service 要分别取数并对齐到同一个 step，否则图上会出现断层或密度突变。代价是聚合语义要小心，平均的平均是错的。
why_en: The two halves of one curve come from different resolutions, so fetch each and align them to a common step, remembering that an average of averages is not a valid aggregate.
tradeoff: 多分辨率带来的存储与查询节省 vs 拼接与聚合语义的复杂度
whenOtherWins: 如果查询范围完全落在 raw 保留期以内，直接读单一分辨率更简单也更准。

termDefinitions.meaning: 查询返回结果的时间桶宽度，比如 60 秒一个点，决定曲线的横向密度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Step is the width of each time bucket in the query result, such as one point per sixty seconds, which sets the density of the curve.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个数据点覆盖多长时间，10 秒档比 1 小时档细，但保留期更短。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Resolution is how much time a single data point covers; a ten-second tier is finer than an hourly tier but is retained for less time.

scenario: 每多建一档 rollup 就多一份存储和后台计算，团队要挑出哪些 metric 值得建 1 分钟档。
scenario_en: Every extra rollup tier costs more storage and background computation, so the team must pick which metrics deserve a one-minute tier.
q: 该拿什么依据来决定建哪些 rollup？
q_en: What should decide which rollups get built?
options: 给所有 metric 都建全部档位，一视同仁最省心
看用户查询历史里哪些 metric 和时间范围最常被查
按 metric 名字母序取前 20% 建档，其余暂时不建
按写入量最大的那些 metric 建，写得多说明它重要
options_en: Build every tier for every metric; treating them uniformly is simplest.
Look at query history for which metrics and time ranges are actually queried most.
Sort metric names alphabetically and build tiers for the first twenty percent.
Build for the highest-write metrics, since high write volume means importance.
optionExplanations: 全量建档把存储和后台计算按档数成倍放大，而多数档位其实从没人查过。
查询历史直接给出真实的时间范围分布，预计算才落在真会被命中的地方。
字母序和访问模式毫无关系，等于随机挑，命中率完全不可控。
写得多只说明上报频繁，很多高频指标只被告警规则读，没人开图看。
optionExplanations_en: Building every tier multiplies storage and background compute by the number of tiers, and most tiers are never queried.
Query history directly reveals the real distribution of time ranges, so precomputation lands where it will be hit.
Alphabetical order has nothing to do with access patterns, making hit rate effectively random.
High write volume only means frequent reporting; many such metrics are read only by alert rules, never opened in a chart.
why: rollup 只有被查到才省时间，所以要用查询历史而不是写入量来选：写得多不等于被查得多。代价是要额外维护一条查询日志的分析链路。
why_en: A rollup only saves time if it is queried, so query history rather than write volume should choose the tiers, at the cost of maintaining a query-log analysis pipeline.
tradeoff: 预计算的存储与计算成本 vs 查询延迟
whenOtherWins: 新上线还没有查询历史时，只能先按常见时间范围铺一套默认档位再观察。

termDefinitions.meaning: 提前把聚合结果算好存起来，用写入时的成本换查询时的延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precomputation stores aggregates ahead of time, spending write-side cost to buy lower query latency.

scenario: 上千人盯着同一张 dashboard、每 10 秒刷新一次，相邻两次查询覆盖的数据几乎完全重叠，只差最后 10 秒。
scenario_en: Thousands of people watch the same dashboard refreshing every ten seconds, so consecutive queries cover almost identical data and differ only in the last ten seconds.
q: 结果缓存的 key 和 TTL 该怎么定？
q_en: How should the result cache key and TTL be defined?
options: key 只用 query 文本，时间范围忽略掉不进 key
key 用 query 加时间范围，TTL 对齐新鲜度要求
key 用查看者的用户 id，每个人各存一份自己的
key 用 query 加时间范围，但永不过期直到人工清理
options_en: Key on query text only and leave the time range out of the key.
Key on query plus time range, with a TTL matched to the freshness requirement.
Key on the viewer user id so every person keeps their own copy.
Key on query plus time range but never expire until someone clears it manually.
optionExplanations: 同一条 query 查昨天和查今天结果完全不同，漏掉时间范围会返回张冠李戴的图。
两者都进 key 才唯一确定一份结果，TTL 则决定用户最多看到多旧的数据。
按用户切分把命中率打到接近零，恰好抹掉上千人看同一张图这个最大红利。
永不过期意味着永远返回第一次算出的那份，用户再也看不到新写进来的点。
optionExplanations_en: The same query over yesterday and over today returns different results, so omitting the range serves the wrong chart.
Both parts together uniquely identify one result, while the TTL decides how stale a user may ever see.
Keying per user drives hit rate near zero, destroying the very benefit of thousands sharing one chart.
Never expiring means always returning the first computed copy, so newly written points never appear.
why: 一份结果的唯一标识 = query + 时间窗，两者都必须进 key；TTL 必须短于用户能接受的滞后，否则缓存会把陈旧的图当成新鲜的返回。
why_en: A result is identified by query plus time window, so both belong in the key, and the TTL must stay shorter than the staleness users are willing to tolerate.
tradeoff: 缓存命中率 vs 数据新鲜度
whenOtherWins: 事故排查要看最近几分钟的数据时，应该让这段查询直接绕过缓存打到数据库。

termDefinitions.meaning: 生存时间：缓存条目自动失效前能存活多久，决定用户可能看到的最大滞后。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL, or time to live, is how long a cache entry survives before expiring, which bounds how stale a user can see.

scenario: 评审 HA 方案时有人提议：给整个监控平台做一套统一的重试与降级策略，摄取和告警都套用它。
scenario_en: During the availability review someone proposes one unified retry and degradation policy applied to both the ingestion path and the alerting path.
q: 为什么摄取路径和告警路径要分开设计恢复策略？
q_en: Why must the ingestion path and the alerting path get separate recovery strategies?
options: 因为两条路径共用同一个 Kafka topic，本来就无法分开
摄取怕数据进不来，告警怕事件发不出去，失败形态不同
因为告警路径的数据吞吐量远远高于摄取路径的吞吐量
因为只有摄取路径需要高可用，告警可以事后补发就行
options_en: Because both paths share one Kafka topic and cannot be separated anyway.
Ingestion fears data not arriving; alerting fears events not going out — different failure shapes.
Because the alerting path carries far more throughput than the ingestion path.
Because only ingestion needs high availability; alerts can be re-sent afterwards.
optionExplanations: 告警事件写的是另一条 topic，两条链路本来就可以独立设计和独立扩缩。
前者靠 agent 缓冲加复制加幂等写救，后者靠 checkpoint 加先落盘加重试救。
摄取是 5M 点/秒的持续洪流，告警事件每分钟才几条，差着几个数量级。
事故时最不能失灵的恰恰是告警，晚发的通知已经错过了它该起作用的时刻。
optionExplanations_en: Alert events go to a different topic, so the two chains can be designed and scaled independently.
The first is saved by agent buffering, replication, and idempotent writes; the second by checkpointing, persisting events first, and retries.
Ingestion is a continuous five-million-points-per-second flood while alert events are a handful per minute, orders of magnitude apart.
Alerting is exactly what must not fail during an incident, since a late page has already missed the moment it mattered.
why: 摄取的失败是「数据进不来」，用缓冲、复制和幂等写解决；告警的失败是「事件发不出去」，用 checkpoint、先落盘再投递和重试解决。代价是要维护两套机制。
why_en: Ingestion fails by data not arriving, fixed with buffering and idempotent writes; alerting fails by events not going out, fixed with checkpoints and persist-before-send.
tradeoff: 两套独立恢复机制的复杂度 vs 单一策略留下的盲区
whenOtherWins: 规模很小、全部组件都单实例部署时，一套统一重试策略已经够用，不值得拆两条路径。

termDefinitions.meaning: 检查点：把流处理的中间状态定期存盘，节点崩溃后可以从这一点续跑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint periodically persists a stream processor state so it can resume from that point after a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 里的一条命名消息流，不同用途的数据通常各走各的 topic。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Kafka topic is a named message stream, and data with different purposes usually flows through separate topics.

scenario: 摄取延迟涨到 90 秒、告警评估慢了 20 秒，值班工程师盯着图却不知道该不该触发降级。
scenario_en: Ingestion lag has grown to ninety seconds and alert evaluation is twenty seconds behind, and the on-call engineer cannot tell whether to trigger degradation.
q: 要让值班能当场判断是否降级，系统还缺什么？
q_en: What is missing so on-call can decide about degrading on the spot?
options: 给所有组件统一加一层自动重试就已经足够了
给每条路径写明 SLO：可容忍的延迟与丢失上限
让值班凭经验判断，把口头约定写进 runbook 即可
把全部延迟指标都画到同一张大 dashboard 上盯着
options_en: Just add one uniform automatic retry layer across all components.
Write an explicit SLO per path: tolerable latency and tolerable loss.
Let on-call judge from experience and put the convention in a runbook.
Put every latency metric on one big shared dashboard and watch it.
optionExplanations: 重试改变的是系统怎么自救，回答不了「现在这个延迟算不算已经坏了」。
告警 1 分钟内触发是需求给定的目标而非算出来的结果，正好可以当阈值。
凭经验意味着不同的人给出不同答案，事故里最不需要的就是这种不确定性。
看得见延迟和知道延迟超标是两回事，图上没那条线就仍然没有判据。
optionExplanations_en: Retries change how the system heals itself; they cannot answer whether the current lag already counts as broken.
Alerts firing within one minute is a given product target rather than a derived number, and it serves directly as the threshold.
Judging from experience means different people give different answers, and an incident is the worst place for that.
Seeing the latency and knowing it is out of bounds are different; without a drawn threshold there is still no criterion.
why: 「90 秒算不算坏」只有对着目标才有答案，所以每条路径先定 SLO，降级才有可判定的触发条件。代价是每条路径都要单独做元监控来测量它。
why_en: Whether ninety seconds is bad only has an answer against a target, so each path needs its own SLO before degradation is decidable, at the cost of separate meta-monitoring.
tradeoff: 明确 SLO 带来的可判定性 vs 定义和元监控的维护成本
whenOtherWins: 早期只有一条路径、一个团队值班时，口头约定也能跑，写 SLO 的收益还不明显。

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：对某条路径承诺的延迟或可用性上限，是判断是否降级的标尺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO, or service level objective, is the latency or availability target promised for a path, and it is the yardstick for deciding to degrade.

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控监控系统自身健康度的那一层，必须独立于被监控的系统之外。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Meta-monitoring is the layer that watches the health of the monitoring system itself and must live outside it.

scenario: 某条 alert 的底层查询跑超时了，evaluator 静静跳过这一轮也没有报错，客户以为「没收到告警就是没事」。
scenario_en: One alert rule underlying query timed out, the evaluator silently skipped that cycle without erroring, and the customer assumes no alert means nothing is wrong.
q: 怎么兜住这种「静默失败」？
q_en: How do you cover this kind of silent failure?
options: 把 evaluator 的查询超时时间从 30 秒调大到 10 分钟
加一个 watchdog：查询超时或数据延迟时主动通知客户
让 evaluator 遇到评估失败时自动把该告警标记成 firing
用同一套监控平台去监控 evaluator 自身的健康度
options_en: Raise the evaluator query timeout from thirty seconds to ten minutes.
Add a watchdog that proactively notifies customers when queries time out or data lags.
Have the evaluator auto-mark the alert as firing whenever evaluation fails.
Use the same monitoring platform to monitor the evaluator own health.
optionExplanations: 把超时调大只是让这一轮拖更久，超时终究会再发生，还拖垮下一轮评估。
它把「我可能没在看」本身变成一条通知，客户就不会误把沉默当成健康。
一失败就报 firing 会把每次查询抖动变成误报，很快没人再认真看这条告警。
监控系统自己挂掉时这条链路一起失灵，正是事故里最典型的一起失明。
optionExplanations_en: A longer timeout only stretches this cycle; the timeout recurs anyway and now delays the next evaluation too.
It turns "I might not be looking" into a notification, so customers stop reading silence as health.
Firing on every failure turns query jitter into false pages, and people soon stop taking that alert seriously.
When the monitoring system itself goes down this path fails with it, which is the classic way teams go blind.
why: 「没有告警」有两种含义：真没事，或系统没在看。watchdog 把后者显式化成一条通知，代价是多一类可能误报的元告警要维护。
why_en: No alert can mean either nothing is wrong or nobody is looking, so a watchdog makes the second case explicit, at the cost of another class of meta-alert that can itself be noisy.
tradeoff: 漏报风险 vs 元告警噪音
whenOtherWins: 如果告警链路已有端到端的合成心跳测试覆盖，watchdog 的边际价值就低了。

termDefinitions.meaning: 看门狗服务：独立于主链路，在评估超时或数据延迟时主动发出兜底通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A watchdog is a service outside the main path that proactively notifies when evaluation times out or data falls behind.

termDefinitions.meaning: 组件出错但没有对外报错，外部看到的只是「什么都没发生」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A silent failure is when a component breaks without surfacing an error, so from outside it looks like nothing happened.

scenario: http_requests 因为带上了 endpoint 和 status_code 标签而被拆成 5000 万条 series，现在用户查「全站总请求数」。
scenario_en: Adding endpoint and status code labels split http_requests into fifty million series, and a user now asks for the total request count across the whole site.
q: 这次查询在读路径上会怎么退化？
q_en: How does that query degrade on the read path?
options: 写入侧索引会膨胀，但读路径不会有额外代价
要把全部 5000 万条 series 读出来相加才得到一个数
TSDB 会自动用 rollup 把它压成一条曲线，秒级返回
查询会直接失败，因为标签数量超过了协议的上限
options_en: Write-side indexes bloat, but the read path pays nothing extra.
All fifty million series must be read and summed to produce one number.
The TSDB automatically collapses it into one curve via rollups and returns instantly.
The query fails outright because the label count exceeds a protocol limit.
optionExplanations: 高基数是双面的：写侧索引和内存涨，读侧的聚合扇入也同样被撑大。
series 数就是这次聚合的扇入宽度，5000 万条都要读进来，耗时线性增长。
rollup 压的是同一条 series 在时间上的点数，压不掉跨 series 的条数。
标签数并没超限，问题是组合出来的 series 太多，查询是慢而不是被拒。
optionExplanations_en: High cardinality cuts both ways: write-side indexes and memory grow, and read-side aggregation fan-in grows with them.
The series count is the fan-in width of this aggregation, so all fifty million must be read and time grows linearly.
Rollups compress points along time within a series; they cannot reduce how many series exist.
The label count is not over any limit; the problem is how many combinations exist, so the query is slow rather than rejected.
why: 高基数不只是写侧的索引和内存开销：任何跨 series 的聚合都要把每条 series 读出来再相加，series 条数直接就是这次查询的扇入宽度。
why_en: High cardinality is not only write-side index and memory cost: any cross-series aggregation reads every series, so the series count is the fan-in width of the query.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 metric 下唯一 series 的数量，由标签组合数决定，直接决定读写代价。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of unique series under a metric, driven by label combinations, and it directly drives both read and write cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次聚合需要读入并合并的来源条数，这里就是参与求和的 series 数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-in is how many sources one aggregation must read and merge, here the number of series being summed.

scenario: 给 http_requests 设 series cap：设 50 万时开发抱怨有用的标签被丢掉，设 5000 万时 TSDB 内存又扛不住。
scenario_en: Setting a series cap on http_requests: at five hundred thousand developers complain useful labels get dropped, and at fifty million the TSDB runs out of memory.
q: 这个上限该怎么定才不会两头挨打？
q_en: How should that cap be set so it fails on neither side?
options: 统一取一个全局默认值，所有 metric 都一视同仁地套用它
逐个 metric 按真实用法调，并盯 dropped 计数
干脆不设上限，让 TSDB 自己扛住多少就算多少
把上限设成 0，禁止任何新的 series 被创建出来
options_en: Pick one global default and apply it uniformly to every metric.
Tune per metric against real usage, watching the dropped counter as feedback.
Set no cap at all and let the TSDB absorb whatever comes.
Set the cap to zero so no new series can ever be created.
optionExplanations: 同一个数字对低基数指标过松、对爆炸型指标过紧，两类都照顾不到。
哪条策略在真丢数据，dropped 计数会直接告诉你，调参因此有了闭环。
不设限就是把内存和写性能交给用户随手加的一个标签来决定。
上限为 0 会连正常的新实例上线都挡住，等于把这个指标冻死。
optionExplanations_en: One number is too loose for low-cardinality metrics and too tight for explosive ones, serving neither.
The dropped counter shows exactly which policy is discarding real data, which closes the tuning loop.
No cap hands memory and write performance over to whatever label a user casually adds.
A cap of zero blocks even legitimate new instances from appearing, freezing the metric entirely.
why: 太严会丢掉真正在用的标签，太松就防不住爆炸，所以只能按每个 metric 的实际用法定，并用 dropped_metrics 计数作为调参反馈。代价是长期的人工运营。
why_en: Too strict drops labels people rely on and too loose lets cardinality explode, so caps are tuned per metric using the dropped-metrics counter as ongoing feedback.
tradeoff: 数据完整性 vs 基数可控性
whenOtherWins: 全新且用量未知的 metric，先给一个宽松上限观察一段时间，比一刀切更安全。

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 metric 允许存在的唯一 series 数上限，超过后新 series 的点被丢弃。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A series cap is the maximum number of unique series allowed per metric, beyond which points for new series are dropped.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录被基数策略丢掉多少数据点的计数器，本身也是一条要监控的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The dropped-metrics counter records how many points the cardinality policy discarded, and it is itself a metric worth monitoring.

scenario: 每个 pod 各自上报了自己的 p99 latency，用户现在想看整个服务（几百个 pod 合起来）的 p99。
scenario_en: Each pod reports its own p99 latency, and a user now wants the p99 for the whole service across hundreds of pods.
q: 为什么不能把各 pod 的 p99 直接平均？
q_en: Why can you not simply average each pod p99?
options: 各 pod 的 p99 平均之后一定偏低，乘 1.2 修正即可
百分位不可加，要在 histogram 上合并后重新算
只要参与合并的 pod 数量是偶数就可以直接平均
其实可以直接平均，这点误差在工程上可以忽略
options_en: Averaging pod p99s always comes out low, so multiply by one point two to correct it.
Percentiles are not additive; merge the histograms and recompute.
It is fine to average as long as the number of pods being merged is even.
You can just average it; the error is negligible in engineering practice.
optionExplanations: 偏差方向取决于各 pod 的流量和分布形状，没有一个固定系数能修正它。
合并的是分布本身：把各 pod 的桶计数相加，再在合并后的分布上找分位点。
pod 数量的奇偶跟分位数的数学性质毫无关系，这是凭空造出来的规则。
一个只占 1% 流量却极慢的 pod 会被平均稀释掉，整体 p99 被严重低估。
optionExplanations_en: The direction of the error depends on each pod traffic and distribution shape, so no fixed factor corrects it.
What merges is the distribution itself: sum the bucket counts, then locate the percentile on the merged distribution.
Whether the pod count is even has nothing to do with the mathematics of percentiles; the rule is invented.
One very slow pod carrying one percent of traffic gets diluted away, badly underestimating the true p99.
why: 百分位是分布上的一个位置，不是可相加的量；要跨 series 求 p99，必须存下 histogram 或 sketch，把桶计数合并后再取分位点。代价是每条 series 的存储明显变大。
why_en: A percentile is a position on a distribution, not an additive quantity, so a cross-series p99 needs merged histogram buckets, which costs more storage per series.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直方图：按值区间统计落入每个桶的次数，桶计数可以跨来源相加后再求分位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A histogram counts how many observations fall into each value bucket, and bucket counts from different sources can be summed before computing a percentile.

termDefinitions.meaning: 概要结构：用远小于原始数据的空间近似估计分位数，并且支持多份合并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sketch is a compact structure that approximates percentiles using far less space than raw data and supports merging multiple copies.

scenario: 平台被多个团队共用。某团队一条 30 天全量查询把 query service 打满，其他团队的 dashboard 集体超时。
scenario_en: The platform is shared by many teams, and one team full thirty-day query saturates the query service, timing out every other team dashboards.
q: 该怎么防止一个租户拖垮其他租户？
q_en: How do you stop one tenant from taking down the others?
options: 把 query service 的实例数直接翻倍就能扛过去
给每个租户设查询与基数配额，并隔离资源池
让受影响的团队自己不断重试，直到查询能成功
把所有租户的数据合并进同一批大 series 一起查
options_en: Just double the number of query service instances.
Give each tenant query and cardinality quotas, and isolate resource pools.
Let affected teams keep retrying until their query eventually succeeds.
Merge all tenants data into one big set of shared series and query together.
optionExplanations: 翻倍只是把同一条重查询的天花板抬高一点，下一条更大的查询照样打满。
配额把「一个租户能消耗多少」变成显式上限，故障半径就被关在他自己那格。
重试在资源已经被占满时只会加剧拥塞，把一次慢查询放大成一场雪崩。
合并数据让租户之间彼此可见，既没解决争抢又直接踩到隔离和权限问题。
optionExplanations_en: Doubling only raises the ceiling a little, and the next larger query saturates it again.
Quotas turn how much one tenant may consume into an explicit bound, confining the blast radius to that tenant.
Retrying while resources are already saturated deepens congestion, turning one slow query into a cascade.
Merging data makes tenants visible to each other, solving nothing about contention and breaking isolation and permissions.
why: 共享的是查询算力和 series 预算，不做配额时最贵的那个租户就替所有人定义了延迟。隔离的代价是资源利用率下降，还要长期运营配额。
why_en: Tenants share query compute and series budget, so without quotas the most expensive tenant defines everyone else latency, and isolation costs utilisation plus admin.
tradeoff: 租户隔离性 vs 资源利用率
whenOtherWins: 单团队自用、负载可预测时，配额纯粹是开销，先不做也不会伤到谁。

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一套系统同时服务多个互不信任的团队或客户，共享底层资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-tenancy means one system serves several mutually untrusting teams or customers on shared underlying resources.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次故障能波及的范围，隔离手段的目标就是把它压到最小。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blast radius is how far one failure spreads, and isolation exists to keep it as small as possible.
